title: The First Letter of John Timeline
sub: Walking in the Light · Tests of Genuine Faith and Love
desc: Written against teachers denying Christ, this letter offers a set of repeated tests for authentic faith (confession over denial, obedience over claim, love over hatred) anchored in the flat statement that God himself is love.

eras.label: Era One · 1 John 1
eras.name: Fellowship in the Light
eras.dates: An eyewitness opens not with a greeting but a declaration, something heard, seen, and touched with his own hands

events.title: The Word of Life: Heard, Seen, Touched
events.detail: John opens without a formal greeting, stacking sensory verbs (heard, seen, beheld, touched) to insist the eternal life he proclaims was a real, physical encounter, not an abstract idea.

verses.text: “What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we beheld and touched with our hands, concerning the Word of Life.”

events.title: God Is Light: If We Confess Our Sins
events.detail: The letter's first thesis statement: God is light with no darkness at all, so claiming fellowship with him while walking in darkness is a lie, but honest confession meets a God who is faithful and righteous to forgive.

verses.text: “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and righteous to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”

eras.label: Era Two · 1 John 2
eras.name: Keeping His Commandments — The Last Hour
eras.dates: An advocate for sinners, an old commandment made new, and a first warning about antichrists already loose in the world

events.title: An Advocate With the Father
events.detail: Written so believers won't sin, but realistic that they will: Jesus Christ himself serves as advocate and propitiation, not only for the readers but for the whole world.

verses.text: “We have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; and He Himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for those of the whole world.”

events.title: An Old Commandment, Made New: Love and Hate for a Brother
events.detail: The command to love isn't new, it's as old as what they first heard, yet it becomes new again as darkness gives way to true light, tested by whether a person loves or hates their brother.

verses.text: “The one who loves his brother abides in the Light… but the one who hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness, and does not know where he is going.”

events.title: Children, Fathers, Young Men: Do Not Love the World
events.detail: John addresses three groups by spiritual maturity, then pivots to a warning: the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life are not from the Father, and the whole world, with its desires, is passing away.

verses.text: “The world is passing away, and also its lusts, but the one who does the will of God abides forever.”

events.title: The Last Hour: Many Antichrists Have Appeared
events.detail: John names the crisis behind the letter: people who once belonged to the community have left, denying that Jesus is the Christ: proof, he says, that they never truly belonged, and a sign the last hour has already arrived.

verses.text: “They went out from us, but they were not really of us; for if they were of us, they would have remained with us.”
“Who is the liar but the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, the one who denies the Father and the Son.”

eras.label: Era Three · 1 John 3
eras.name: Children of God — Love in Deed and Truth
eras.dates: An identity already given, tested against Cain's example, and defined as action rather than sentiment

events.title: Called Children of God
events.detail: John marvels at the love that makes believers God's own children now, with a future not yet fully revealed, but certain enough that the hope itself produces present purity.

verses.text: “See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we would be called children of God; and we are.”

events.title: Sin Is Lawlessness: Born of God Does Not Sin
events.detail: A stark, much-debated passage: those born of God cannot go on sinning, because his seed abides in them: the dividing line between children of God and children of the devil is drawn at practiced, habitual sin versus righteousness.

verses.text: “Everyone who has been born of God does not sin, because His seed abides in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.”

events.title: Not Like Cain: Laying Down Our Lives for the Brothers
events.detail: Cain becomes the negative example of love: he murdered his brother because his own deeds were evil. Christ's own self-giving becomes the positive standard: love proven not in word but in concrete deed and truth.

verses.text: “By this we have known love, that He laid down His life for us; and we ought to lay down our lives for the brothers.”
“Let us not love with word or with tongue, but in deed and truth.”

events.title: Confidence Before God: Keeping His Commandments
events.detail: When the heart condemns, John says God is greater than the heart and knows all things: confidence in prayer and assurance of God's abiding presence come through obedience and the Spirit given to believers.

verses.text: “God is greater than our heart and knows all things.”

eras.label: Era Four · 1 John 4
eras.name: Test the Spirits — God Is Love
eras.dates: A practical test for competing claims to inspiration, grounded in the letter's most famous definition of God's own character

events.title: Test the Spirits: Confessing Jesus Come in the Flesh
events.detail: With false prophets active, John gives a concrete doctrinal test: any spirit confessing Jesus Christ came in the flesh is from God, any that denies it carries the spirit of antichrist.

verses.text: “Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God, and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God.”

events.title: God Is Love: He Sent His Son as Propitiation
events.detail: One of the Bible's most quoted definitions of God: love isn't just something God does, it's what he is: proven not by human affection for God but by God's initiative in sending his Son for sins.

verses.text: “The one who does not love does not know God, because God is love.”
“In this is love, not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins.”

events.title: Perfect Love Casts Out Fear
events.detail: Abiding in God's love produces confidence rather than fear on the day of judgment, and John closes with a test that can't be dodged: anyone claiming to love a God they haven't seen while hating a brother they have is simply lying.

verses.text: “There is no fear in love; but perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves punishment.”
“If someone says, ‘I love God,’ and hates his brother, he is a liar; for the one who does not love his brother whom he has seen, cannot love God whom he has not seen.”

eras.label: Era Five · 1 John 5
eras.name: Overcoming the World — The Testimony of God
eras.dates: Faith as the victory that overcomes the world, three witnesses in agreement, and a closing warning as blunt as the letter's opening was intimate

events.title: Born of God Overcomes the World: Our Faith
events.detail: Belief that Jesus is the Christ marks the new birth, and John identifies the very thing that overcomes the world not as strength or effort but simply as faith itself.

verses.text: “Everything that has been born of God overcomes the world; and this is the overcoming that has overcome the world—our faith.”

events.title: The Water and the Blood: Three Witnesses in Agreement
events.detail: A dense, much-discussed passage names three witnesses to Jesus's identity (the Spirit, the water, and the blood) arguing that if human testimony is trusted, God's own testimony about his Son carries far greater weight.

verses.text: “God gave us eternal life, and this life is in His Son. He who has the Son has the life; he who does not have the Son of God does not have that life.”

events.title: Confidence in Prayer: Sin Leading to Death
events.detail: John states his purpose for writing plainly, so readers can know they have eternal life, and addresses confidence in prayer, along with a difficult, much-debated distinction between sin that leads to death and sin that doesn't.

verses.text: “These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, so that you may know that you have eternal life.”

events.title: Closing: ‘Guard Yourselves From Idols’
events.detail: Three confident 'we know' statements close the letter's argument, before an abrupt final line that seems to shift subject entirely: a plain warning against idols, closing a letter that spent five chapters on love and truth.

verses.text: “Little children, guard yourselves from idols.” — an abrupt closing line, likely aimed at the same false teaching addressed throughout the letter.
